lines.e1: etcd is the database of Kubernetes: every object, from pods to secrets, is stored there.
lines.e2: It is a key-value store: each object lives under a key, built from its type, namespace and name.
lines.e3: Several etcd members form a cluster and elect a leader. Only the leader accepts writes.
lines.e4: A write is committed once a majority of members have it. This is the Raft algorithm.
lines.e5: That is why clusters run three or five members. With three, one can fail and the cluster still has a quorum.
lines.e6: Clients can watch a key, and etcd pushes every change. That is how the scheduler, controllers and kubelets react in real time.
lines.e7: Lose etcd without a backup, and you lose the cluster state. So take regular snapshots.
